state.question: Which video connects its central mystery to a destroyed physical object?
state.summary: Fresh projection: v3 is the only video with local evidence of a damaged/defaced physical portrait connected to investigative review, while v1/v2/v4 lack observed destroyed-object links and v2/v4 gaps are not negative evidence. Despite unresolved uncertainty about whether the portrait is primary, it is the best-supported option.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

attempts: v3 repeatedly shows a framed portrait with yellow paint smeared across the face and CCTV review of the same defaced portrait, making it the strongest candidate for a mystery tied to a damaged physical object; whether this is central rather than incidental vandalism remains uncertain.
The portrait appears on a monitor and in close-up, but the current evidence does not establish whether it is the primary object under review or merely displayed while another mystery is central.
v2 and v4 have unobserved intervals that cannot be treated as absence; no observed destroyed physical object linked to their central mysteries is available in the current evidence.
